breakpoints.note: The PoC's chunked operations include publish actions with matching topic names, so execution reaches the subscriber iteration loop inside publish() where message indices are recorded and drain is triggered.

The subscriber's message index is materialized from the current outgoingMessages vector size during publish(). This index is valid at creation but becomes a stale out-of-bounds value after the linked-list corruption causes the subscriber to be orphaned and a subsequent drain clears the vector.

When the subscriber being individually drained is the head of drainableSubscribers, the code sets drainableSubscribers to nullptr instead of s->next. This orphans all subsequent subscribers in the doubly-linked list: they retain numMessageIndices > 0 and stale messageIndices but are unreachable from the list head. The same bug exists in freeSubscriber at line 233. The patch introduces unlinkDrainableSubscriber() that correctly sets drainableSubscribers to s->next.

drainImpl reads outgoingMessages at the orphaned subscriber's stale message index. The index exceeds the vector's current size (0 after clear) but falls within its allocated capacity. ASan detects the 1-byte read of a std::string in the container-overflow zone when the drain callback calls message.length().
